channel.title: Site Status
channel.description: Feed for status of www.rapidcow.org and other sites.

item.title: Update
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
(Old Message on Wed, 18 Dec 2024 13:29:23 -0600)

Hello hello! Good morning! ^^ (or afternoon I guess =.=)

So last night I couldn't sleep so I went though the rest of server nginx logs… stayed up quite late but in the end it was worth it I guess? At least now I get to see just how many bots are visiting and put their stats up in the hall of shame (mwehehe >:)

(New message)

Hiya so, now that I am hosting the status page myself, I can say I am quite disappointed. Within mere seconds my logs were instantaneously flooded with requests that blatantly probe for server vulnerability—paths like /.env and /wp-whatever and such. I forgot what they were exactly but they made me feel sick….

Also in case it isn't obvious enough already, every other site is still technically "down" even though the server isn't; for a while you could make requests to rapidcow.org and it would just give you a bad host error (because I disabled all my old configs and naturally nginx wouldn't recognize any virtual host other than status.rapidcow.org.) To prevent that confusion I have since removed DNS records that pointed rapidcow.org and www.rapidcow.org to my server, so now you get an DNS error instead of a scary bad host error. I haven't done that for all domains though; but I'm tired…

About the plans? Forget about it… I need to rest my eyes…. My flight back home is in less than 48 hours. I can probably look to measures to ban these bots more effectively than directly looking at the access logs (grep'ing their IPs in existing blacklists is an idea). But I won't be updating this until I'm back home….

(Sorry, it's just… the dead Internet thing feels too real. Maybe only now am I seeing it for what it is. Why did I want to make a website again? Maybe I can just turn it off when I'm tired and turn it back on when I'm not… It feels like no one's there… (or maybe I could just switch to Neocities so I don't have to experience despair from staring at the abysmal amount of bot requests))

item.title: I need more time :(
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
Yeah, I definitely underestimated what could happen over a day rather than how long it practically takes to do the thing. You never know what will get in the way. And eating more than I wanted definitely did not help my stomach, aeugh... (they even got me the wrong bao and I couldn't even complain :<)

(Life tip: if you do not want to eat more than a bowl of noodles and you see people ordering a bunch of things, *do not* order more than that bowl of noodles! Otherwise -- well there is no otherwise; you'll just suffer...)

Also I have an exam in 30 minutes it's computer science but they ask annoying questions that I don't know if I will get right, then there's math tomorrow that I think I will need to pay a little more attention to... I don't know there's just so much to do!!! >n<

But I did write a something that made updating this feed easier? I pushed that new branch to Codeberg yesterday, so you can see how it's done. It uses Perl which I think is an underrated language full of code written by people who enjoy the craft. Really—I was reading Template::Tutorials::Datafile and many other perldocs yesterday. I am really glad to see this art isn't lost to time and completely displaced by huge corporate codebases. :)

(Every time I say something that doesn't really have to do with the announcement, haha... but this is my website! It's kind of the point that I get to talk about what I want to talk about. XD)

Oh right, and if I were to name a new time.... Let's try Wednesday in my time alright :) We'll see how things go...

item.title: Extended Maintenance
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
Argh can't believe it's 24-hours already... sorry. :( I wasn't doing just the web site thing. It's just I've never had this much free time, I had to catch up with some backing up personal stuff, and that involved hours of yelling at git-annex to stop being so paranoid about copying and deleting my files from Google Drive... and connecting a ton of cables on my bed because some of the files were only on my hard drive, yikes >_>

But I did get a look at the server logs in the end! I do have some experience exporting since I've done that before (a month or so ago), but because it was so tedious last time that I decided to "speed up" the process by making my Bash scripts more robust, and that meant running into more quirky stuff like variable scopes.

And I got up at 5 PM! Okay don't judge me I know I slept for 12 hours >:( it was more than what I expected too, but I am sort of hungry now... so I might have to go and eat something first before continuing.

Also, the CSS for this page is kind of bad: pure white on black/black on white? Old-school terminals used pure white exclusively for BOLD text (it looks something like this); it's like they understand color theory or something! So I might have to change that -- but that's only after I get the sites back up again? Waaahhh I don't knoooow >n<

-- but I know the old blue maintenance page has to go! I thought it'd mostly be the crawlers visiting (so the PNG drawing wouldn't be requested as much), but I fed the 1.5 million logs I exported last time into GoAccess and turns out there were still so many requests for the image! So the new page will have to be MUCH more lightweight (with NO images!) and I don't know, maybe I will call it an "under construction" page to distinguish it from what I am calling maintenance for this ongoing... thing?

But yeah. I will need more time. It'll probably take more than a day to get everything done, but at least I will configure nginx properly this time, set up logrotate and figure out how to export logs in a way that doesn't shut all the ports down again like this, put up the new page for every site that I'm not ready to show -- geesh does that not sound like a lot to you? Being a webmaster is HARD. :c

BUT... it's a battle I am willing to fight. Being a webmaster is fun, even if I know that fewer people will watching compared to when I was on YouTube or Twitter. Having said that I do remember reading a few things that I quite liked: this world needs more webmasters, not influencers, TikToks, social media -- and I definitely don't mean graphic designers and developers!

Yeah right this announcement has been long enough I'll go eat something and then get back to work =n= (ooh and I'm also thinking of publishing some stats from my nginx logs, with individual IP addresses anonymized (obviously)! If you have anything specific you want to see in mind (yes! YOU reading this!!!) send me an e-mail (it's in this RSS feed) and let me know! Otherwise I'll only look into my favorite stats like how much bandwidth I am wasting...)

item.title: Server Downtime [+24 hours]
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
Hi this is rapid!

It's been a while since i cleaned out the nginx logs, now that my finals are out of the way [well, the hard ones for me at least :] But before I do that I prefer to not have to worry about new logs coming in. Stuff like telling nginx where to write the access/error logs and logrotate are going to create a mess if I don't set them up right...

So I decided to schedule a DOWNTIME! Basically, the server will be down for real this time (there wouldn't even be a maintenance page). This affects all sites besides this status and the URL shortener (a.rdks.org), which are the only sites hosted by Codeberg Pages. Though I think no one would be seriously affected by this, so I won't give you too much time prepare.

Things I want to do besides exporting nginx logs include:

  1. set www.rapidcow.org as the canonical domain
  2. clean up my server files scattered over /home and /var/www/ (and update the nginx rules, obviously)
  3. and probably learn how to use logrotate so that I'm not looking at thousands of lines at once... also i want to see how i can do this more regularly and easily (and maybe even get GoAccess to work?)

The exact period of maintenance is... I'm not sure. But the plan is that it would be back within 24 hours of the publish date of this post (so Sat thru Sun, UTC 2 AM). The HTTP(S) ports might get turned on and off during this period (so don't be surprised if you see the sites still running -- I might still be working!) If I need more time than that, I'll let you know :)

Thank you for understanding. It's an honor to be your host of my Web... o7 -RC

item.title: Plans for the end of 2024
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
I got some more motivation to return to this and escape social media hellhole! Thank you to my anonymous friend for being my FIRST subscriber outside of social media :)

The plans are simple: www.rapidcow.org will get a landing page and a home page and www.endfind.me will get just a landing page that double as the home page. (Don't visit either yet though, and if you do, don't be like Twitter.)

The exact date I'm unsure, but it should happen sometime between next week and the week after. I'll let you know that when that happens. Before that though I need to deal with them finals next week (ugh school... DX)

Thanks. I hope I can keep feeling this motivated.

item.title: Update: Neocities
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
I made a Neocities account and wrote more than I ever intended to even for www.rapidcow.org o_o

Looks like signing up for Neocities was the right choice, but well, now I'm exhausted… and I need some sleep….

(if you are curious about it now, head over to https://rapidcow.neocities.org. i sat in front of my laptop for ~4 hours just to write up a good-enough answer — i did NOT expect it to go like this.)
